criteria.name: Introduction — Identifies ethical issues and broad links to engineering design. Discusses context of ethical issues in engineering organisations. Identifies the relevant stakeholders when considering the ethical issues.
criteria.reasoning: Several issues identified (safety vs business, QA time pressure) linked to engineering design and engineering organisations. Stakeholders comprehensively listed including end-users, with significance explained.

evidence.quote: maintaining product quality safety while trying to succeed as a business in a competitive field.
relevant stakeholders in this scenario include Rachel, Rachel's company, the chip contract company, the government health department
many people who will use, be affected by, or rely on the services of the government health department.

criteria.name: Balanced Discussion — Discusses objective arguments for and against decisions of the ethical issues. Draws a conclusion on how stakeholders should make decisions about the issues.
criteria.reasoning: Objective for/against arguments presented with reasonable depth (competitive advantage, revenue, growth vs harm, integrity, fines). Conclusion drawn for stakeholders but decision recommendations not differentiated per stakeholder, leaning on personal ethical stance.

criteria.name: Compelling Argument that supports conclusion — The report forms a compelling argument, which justifies the conclusion. The body of the report follows a logical structure, with paragraphs linked and content ordered in a way that is easy to follow and support the building of the argument. Arguments demonstrate a systematic understanding of the ethical issues for all stakeholders.
criteria.reasoning: Report follows logical abstract-intro-discussion-path-conclusion-recommendation structure. Argument for not shipping builds systematically through harm, code, reputation cases and supports conclusion. Compelling but could further systematise trade-offs for all stakeholders.

evidence.quote: severity of potential harm to end-users cannot be understated.
decision to Not Ship is certainly the most ethical path.
Rachel should refuse the contract with the government health department.

criteria.reasoning: Uses 4 references and three external case studies (Apple, NHS HSSIB, VW) to substantiate arguments. Qualitative evidence present, but quantitative evidence lacking, references formatting weak, and depth moderate not in-depth balanced research.

technical_issues.where: DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship
technical_issues.issue: Typo in heading and some grammatical errors; no calculation errors but limited quantitative trade-off analysis for revenue vs fines risk.
Malformed URLs and inconsistent Harvard style, missing access details for [3] and [4]. No figures/tables provided.

overall: Clear ethical analysis favouring not shipping, supported by stakeholder identification and external cases. Meets word limit and structure, but needs stronger quantitative evidence, visual support, and refined referencing.

feedback.summary: You produced a clear, well-structured ethics report that argues convincingly for not shipping. You identified key issues in INTRODUCTION, listed stakeholders comprehensively, and used strong cases. To reach Excellent across all criteria, strengthen stakeholder-specific recommendations, add quantitative evidence and visuals, and refine referencing accuracy.
next_steps: In DISCUSSION, add a simple table weighing stakeholders (Rachel, company, health department, end-users) with distinct decision recommendations to reach Excellent in C2 and C3.
Strengthen C4 by adding one quantitative trade-off (e.g., estimated recall/fine cost vs contract revenue) and fix References [3][4] with access dates and consistent Harvard style.
For C5, correct heading typo DICUSSION to DISCUSSION and insert one visual (stakeholder map or risk matrix) to support your argument and move from Good to Very Good.

criteria.C1: You excelled here. In INTRODUCTION you identified several issues like "maintaining product quality safety while trying to succeed as a business" and linked them to engineering design/organisations. You comprehensively listed stakeholders including "many people who will use... services of the government health department." Keep this depth.
criteria.C2: You built objective for/against arguments in DISCUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship covering revenue and competitive advantage versus harm and integrity. Your CONCLUSION that risks are "colossal" follows logically. For Excellent, add tailored decision guidance for each stakeholder, not just Rachel.
criteria.C3: Your structure from ABSTRACT through RECOMMENDATION flows logically and your argument in The Most Ethical Path systematically builds to "decision to Not Ship is certainly the most ethical path." For Excellent, make the trade-offs explicit for all stakeholders to show systematic understanding.
criteria.C4: Good use of qualitative evidence: Apple releases, HSSIB IT failures, and VW emissions scandal in The Most Ethical Path. To reach Very Good, add quantitative evidence as noted in marking and ensure References are consistently formatted with full details.
criteria.C5: Your report has clear sections including ABSTRACT and INTRODUCTION and fluent writing. To reach Very Good, you need visual elements as required, and to correct errors cited in marking such as "DICUSSION" and the malformed URL "Avww" in References.
